concepts.def: Flow of charge per second, measured in amperes (A)
Energy per unit charge, measured in volts (V)
Opposition to current, measured in ohms (Ω)
V = I × R for ohmic conductors at fixed temperature
One single loop — current is the same everywhere
Branches in a loop — each branch shares the voltage

walkthroughs.body_html:
A circuit is a loop where charge can flow. ⚡

Current is how much charge flows per second. It is measured in amperes (A) using an ammeter, which goes in series.

Voltage (also called potential difference) is the energy each unit of charge carries. It is measured in volts (V) using a voltmeter, placed in parallel across a component.

Resistance is how much a component opposes the current. It is measured in ohms (Ω).

Thin wires, long wires, and hot wires all have more resistance. Thick, short, cool wires have less resistance.

A resistor is a component made to have a fixed resistance.

Ohm's law: V = I × R. If V doubles and R stays the same, I doubles too.

In a series circuit there is one loop. The current is the same at every point, but voltage is shared between components.

In a parallel circuit there are branches. Each branch sees the full voltage, but the current splits.

mcqs.q: Which instrument measures current, and how is it connected?
In a series circuit with one battery and two bulbs, what is true about the current?
options: It is largest near the battery
It is zero in one bulb

numericals.q: A 9 V battery drives a current of 3 A through a resistor. What is the resistance, in Ω?
numericals.hint: Rearrange V = I × R to get R = V ÷ I.
